# Tephra

> A DCB-compliant, immutable event store with global ordering, written in Rust. Events carry a
> type and a set of tags; a query reads exactly the events a decision depends on, and the same
> query guards the append. A single writer assigns a dense, monotonic position to every event, so
> the log is one global order and everything else is derived from it. Single node, one logical
> writer per bounded context. It serves its protocol over optional TLS with bearer-token
> authentication, and has official Go, JavaScript, and Rust clients. This documentation tracks the
> current `main`.

## Docs

- [Introduction](https://tephra.tqwewe.com/introduction/): what a Dynamic Consistency Boundary is and the problem it removes, with the course-and-student example.
- [Getting started](https://tephra.tqwewe.com/getting-started/): run the server, connect with tephra-client, append, read, subscribe.
- [Clients](https://tephra.tqwewe.com/clients/): the official Go, JavaScript, and Rust clients and the design they share.
- [Go client](https://tephra.tqwewe.com/clients/go/): connect, append, read, and subscribe from Go with tephra-go.
- [JavaScript client](https://tephra.tqwewe.com/clients/javascript/): connect, append, read, and subscribe from Node.js with @tephradb/client.
- [Rust client](https://tephra.tqwewe.com/clients/rust/): the reference client, blocking or async, with tephra-client.
- [Embedded](https://tephra.tqwewe.com/embedded/): embed the engine directly instead of running the server, and the tradeoffs.
- [Core concepts](https://tephra.tqwewe.com/core-concepts/): events, types and tags, positions, queries, append conditions.
- [Decision models](https://tephra.tqwewe.com/guides/decision-models/): read, fold, decide, append guarded by the same query.
- [The uniqueness guard](https://tephra.tqwewe.com/guides/uniqueness-guard/): omit after to guard that something happens at most once.
- [Subscriptions](https://tephra.tqwewe.com/guides/subscriptions/): catch-up and live-tail as one loop, and resuming from a cursor.
- [Handling conflicts](https://tephra.tqwewe.com/guides/conflicts/): SameBatch is advisory and retryable; Durable is terminal until you rebuild.
- [Operations](https://tephra.tqwewe.com/operations/): configuration, transport security (TLS) and bearer-token authentication, durability, recovery, backpressure, connection limits and reaping, monitoring, shutdown.
- [Architecture](https://tephra.tqwewe.com/architecture/): the layer map and the design rationale, including rejected alternatives.
- [Comparison](https://tephra.tqwewe.com/comparison/): measured write and read comparisons against UmaDB, Axon Server, KurrentDB, and Postgres, including where Tephra loses (cold reads).
- [Status](https://tephra.tqwewe.com/status/): what is built and what is deliberately deferred.
